name: LANSCE-mQ
full_name: LANSCE dedicated milli/fractionally charged particle search
summary: LANSCE-mQ is proposed at LANSCE, Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico. It shares the LANSCE beam environment but is distinct from the CCM liquid-argon detector concept.
detection_principle: An 800 MeV proton fixed target produces candidate small-charge particles. Two scintillator layers seek coincident weak-ionization light signals; on-site background measurements assess neutrons and PMT dark counts.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
